# Curlimp 0.5.1

A native dependency security update. CLI behavior, multiple transfers, response exports, and the 38 browser profiles remain unchanged.

## Security fixes and advisory review

- Backport the [official ngtcp2 qlog fix](https://github.com/ngtcp2/ngtcp2/commit/708a7640c1f48fb8ffb540c4b8ea5b4c1dfb8ee5) for **CVE-2026-40170**, keeping ngtcp2 1.20.0 and its existing impersonation changes.
- Add an AddressSanitizer regression on Linux amd64/arm64 and macOS arm64. The same test reproduced the stack buffer overflow before the fix and passes afterward. Sanitizer instrumentation is confined to temporary test builds.
- Verify that the pinned c-ares 1.34.8 archive retains the upstream fix for **CVE-2026-33630**. The advisory's affected and patched ranges conflict; the reporter records a narrowly scoped source review with primary evidence, rather than ignoring the advisory.
- Reopen triage when reviewed sources, patches, build recipes, or affected/patched metadata change. Unknown advisories and source failures continue to fail the maintenance report.

See [Security: reviewed native advisories](https://github.com/JuanFontes/curlimp/blob/v0.5.1/SECURITY.md#reviewed-native-advisories) for the exact source hashes, upstream commits, and validation scope.

## Update

```sh
docker pull juanfontes/curlimp
docker run --rm juanfontes/curlimp --version
```

For deliberate version selection, use `juanfontes/curlimp:0.5.1` or a digest. Docker images support Linux amd64 and arm64. Native downloads cover both Linux architectures and experimental macOS Apple Silicon; verify `SHA256SUMS` and retain the entire extracted bundle. macOS packages are signed ad hoc and are not notarized.

Browser fingerprint equivalence and HTTP/3 fidelity remain unverified. This security update does not claim otherwise.
